decisions.context: Resolves tension between exposing powerful features early and overwhelming new users with too many choices simultaneously.
options_considered: Bottom tab bar visible from app launch always
Tabs revealed progressively as onboarding milestones complete
decisions.chosen_approach: Unlock navigation tabs incrementally as Marcus completes each onboarding milestone, starting with two core tabs.
decisions.rationale: Hick's Law dictates that reducing initial choices speeds decision-making, directly addressing Marcus Chen's need for immediate directional clarity without cognitive overload.
decisions.trade_offs: Power users like Marcus Chen may feel patronized by gated navigation, requiring clear visual affordances indicating locked tabs are temporary.
decisions.success_metric: Time-to-first-meaningful-action under 90 seconds for 70% of new users in usability testing.

decisions.context: Resolves the premature KYC prompt pain point by demonstrating product value before requesting sensitive personal information.
options_considered: Collect full KYC data before any app exploration permitted
Allow read-only portfolio exploration before triggering KYC prompt
decisions.chosen_approach: Let users explore simulated portfolio and rate data for up to 10 minutes before surfacing a contextual KYC prompt tied to a specific action.
decisions.rationale: Progressive Disclosure supports deferring KYC complexity until Roy Tanner has built enough precarious trust to willingly share sensitive data.
decisions.trade_offs: Deferred KYC increases drop-off risk at the verification step for users who explore but never commit, inflating acquisition cost without conversion.
decisions.success_metric: KYC completion rate above 60% among users who reach the deferred prompt within the first session.

decisions.context: Resolves Diane's frustration with form errors appearing only after full submission, breaking her high-velocity input behavior.
options_considered: Show all validation errors only on form submission tap
Validate each field inline immediately after user leaves focus
decisions.chosen_approach: Validate fields on blur with inline micro-copy that explains the fix in plain language beneath the offending field.
decisions.rationale: Postel's Law—accepting liberal user input and responding with precise, forgiving feedback—directly supports Diane Kowalski's need for speed without punitive re-entry loops.
decisions.trade_offs: Aggressive inline validation on fast-typing users can produce flickering error states that feel accusatory before input is complete.
decisions.success_metric: Form error recovery rate above 85% on first correction attempt without requiring full re-entry.

decisions.context: Resolves the cognitive overload of presenting all account setup requirements on a single dense screen.
options_considered: Single scrollable setup screen with all fields visible at once
Seven discrete screens each containing one to three related fields
decisions.chosen_approach: Group onboarding steps into chunks of no more than three related fields per screen with a persistent progress indicator.
decisions.rationale: Miller's Law—working memory capacity of roughly seven plus or minus two items—justifies chunking to prevent Roy Tanner from abandoning setup due to perceived complexity.
decisions.trade_offs: More screens increases total perceived length of onboarding, which risks frustrating Marcus Chen who prioritizes reaching the core product quickly.
decisions.success_metric: Onboarding abandonment rate below 20% across all seven screens measured via funnel analytics.

decisions.context: Resolves Roy Tanner's precarious trust state by making encryption and data practices visible before he is asked to input any data.
options_considered: Show security certifications only in Settings or footer links
Surface a single prominent trust badge and one-line security statement on the first data-entry screen
decisions.chosen_approach: Display a Von Restorff-isolated trust badge with a one-sentence encryption statement directly above the first personal data field.
decisions.rationale: The Von Restorff Effect ensures the isolated trust badge is memorably distinct, directly countering Roy Tanner's precarious trust state at the highest-anxiety moment of data entry.
decisions.trade_offs: Prominent security framing may signal to lower-anxiety users like Marcus Chen that the app is overly cautious, potentially undermining a perception of seamless modernity.
decisions.success_metric: Trust perception score above 4.0 out of 5.0 on post-onboarding survey question about data safety confidence.

decisions.context: Resolves the pain point of wasted interactive time caused by a mandatory branding animation before the app becomes usable.
options_considered: Retain full 3-second branded splash animation on every cold launch
Replace splash with an instant-render skeleton screen loading real content beneath the logo
decisions.chosen_approach: Replace the splash animation with a static logo visible for no more than 400 milliseconds while content hydrates behind a skeleton screen.
decisions.rationale: The Doherty Threshold—system responses under 400ms maintain user flow state—ensures Marcus Chen experiences immediate interactivity and perceives the app as fast and responsive.
decisions.trade_offs: Removing the branded animation reduces a deliberate aesthetic moment that the Aesthetic-Usability Effect could leverage to build early emotional goodwill with Diane Kowalski.
decisions.success_metric: Perceived load time rated as fast or very fast by at least 80% of users in post-session usability interviews.
